title: Cognitive dissonance
researchPrompt: Explain why people change their beliefs to match their actions rather than the other way round, and what that predicts about persuasion.
suggestedAngles: Treat the discomfort as the mechanism and belief change as the cheapest way to end it
Use the induced-compliance finding: smaller incentives produce larger attitude change
Draw the practical inversion: get someone to act first, and the belief follows

title: The availability heuristic
researchPrompt: Explain why people judge how likely something is by how easily examples come to mind, and why that shortcut is usually right but fails predictably.
suggestedAngles: Frame it as a sensible default that breaks when recall stops tracking frequency
Use media coverage to show how the input can be systematically skewed
Distinguish availability from base-rate neglect rather than blurring them together

references.label: Tversky & Kahneman (1973) — Availability: A Heuristic for Judging Frequency and Probability

title: Why remembering changes the memory
researchPrompt: Explain why recalling an event can alter it, and what that implies about eyewitness testimony and about your own confident memories.
suggestedAngles: Treat memory as reconstruction rather than playback
Use the misinformation effect to show how post-event input gets absorbed
Confront the uncomfortable corollary: confidence does not track accuracy
